newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Rio Tinto combines coal businesses.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Rio Tinto combines coal businesses.

text.p: Coal and Allied Industries Ltd had agreed with its 71 percent owner Rio Tinto Plc/Ltd, formerly RTZ Corp Plc-CRA Ltd, to combine its operational administrative and service functions with Rio Tinto subsidiary Novacoal, Coal and Allied said on Wednesday.
There would be no material transfer of assets out of Coal and Allied or Novacoal, Coal and Allied said.

The combined management company would be called Rio Tinto Coal (NSW) Pty Ltd and its head office would be based in the Hunter Valley, north of Sydney. "Rio Tinto Coal (NSW) will be accountable to the Coal & Allied Board and there will be no material transfer of assets out of Coal & Allied or Novacoal," Coal and Allied's independent directors said in a statement.
"This restructure, which has the agreement of the independent directors, will clear the way for improved performance of our operations," Coal and Allied independent director Derrick Docherty said.
"The savings and operating efficiencies we expect to achieve will help to build shareholder value," he said.
Rio Tinto Coal (NSW) would retain a representative office in Sydney for its marketing departments.
The new company's managing director will be Kim Tronson, who has held senior psositions at Novacoal and Kembla Coal and Coke.
Rio Tinto said in a separate statement the total restructure would result in annual savings to the two companies of more than A$13 million pre tax.

Analysts have said the A$13 million in savings related to savings of about US$1 per tonne of coal produced. Steaming coal prices are currently about US$37.65 a tonne. Coal and Allied produces about 60 percent steaming coal.
"It is no secret that we have not been satisfied with the performance of our New South Wales coal assets," Rio Tinto Energy chief executive Leigh Clifford said in the statement.
"Let there be no confusion -- we are moving this business into the heart of the Hunter Valley for the long haul," he said.
"We are determined to operate these mines efficiently and profitably. This new structure is the first step to improve our performance," he said.
Head office numbers would fall by about 70 and 35 roles would transfer to the Singleton area, Rio Tinto said.
Coal and Allied's shares were untraded at 12.15 p.m. (0215 GMT), having closed down 10 cents at A$9.40 on Tuesday.
